exact_locator: SCC proved in T^3-Gowdy: the generic set G_ic (open in C^1 x C^0 from the earlier paper) is dense in C^1, and its solutions have C^2-inextendible MGHD; the Kretschmann scalar is unbounded along causal curves ending on the singularity.
evidence_excerpt: OpenAlex abstract: '... Here, we prove strong cosmic censorship in the class of T^3-Gowdy spacetimes. In a previous paper, we introduced a set G_ic of smooth initial data and proved that it is open in the C^1 x C^0-topology. The solutions corresponding to initial data in G_ic have the following properties. First, the MGHD is C^2-inextendible. Second, ... the Kretschmann scalar is unbounded along any causal curve that ends on the singularity. The purpose of the present paper is to prove that G_ic is dense in the C^1-topology.'

title: Rough initial data and the strength of the blue-shift instability on cosmological black holes with Lambda > 0
exact_locator: For generic finite-local-energy initial data on subextremal RN-dS (or KN-dS), the linear wave solution has infinite local energy across CH+ and fails to be H^1_loc near any CH+ point.
evidence_excerpt: Theorem 1.1: 'Consider a subextremal Reissner-Nordstrom-de Sitter spacetime, or more generally, Kerr-Newman-de Sitter spacetime M~. For generic initial data (Psi, Psi') with finite local energy along Sigma~, the resulting solution psi of (4) in D^+(Sigma~) has infinite local energy along hypersurfaces intersecting transversally the Cauchy horizon CH+, i.e. psi in particular fails to extend H^1_loc around any point of CH+.'

title: Weak null singularities in general relativity
venue: Journal of the American Mathematical Society 31(1), 1-63 (2018); arXiv:1311.4970
verification_method: arxiv-abs-page + openalex-api (ledger SRC-022 had no arXiv id)
exact_locator: Thm 3: under Thm 2's assumptions the spacetime 'can be extended continuously up to and beyond the singular boundaries'. Thm 4: if the initial data satisfy an integrated non-degeneracy condition, 'the Christoffel symbols ... do not belong to L^2 in a neighborhood of any point' of the boundary. Remark 6 adds that whether the spacetime admits any other continuous extension is an open problem.
evidence_excerpt: Abstract: 'We construct a class of spacetimes (without symmetry assumptions) satisfying the vacuum Einstein equations with singular boundaries on two null hypersurfaces intersecting in the future on a 2-sphere. The metric of these spacetimes extends continuously beyond the singularities while the Christoffel symbols fail to be square integrable in a neighborhood of any point on the singular boundaries. The construction shows moreover that the singularities are stable in a suitable sense.'

title: On the uniqueness of continuous spacetime extensions in 1+1 dimensions with applications to weak null singularities
exact_locator: Thm 4.3: any C0 extension in which the limit p~ exists satisfies one of a list of alternatives (in particular the extension either extends continuously to the boundary or does not). Cor 4.6: for strongly spherically symmetric C0 extensions of subextremal RN across the Cauchy horizon, the extension is locally C0-equivalent to the standard one.
evidence_excerpt: Abstract: 'Motivated by weak null singularities in black hole interiors, we study 1+1 dimensional Lorentzian manifolds (M,g) which admit a continuous spacetime extension across a null boundary v=0 ... Firstly, we find that in general not even the C^0-structure of the extension is uniquely determined by the assumption that the metric extends continuously. However, we exhibit an interesting local-global relation ...'

title: Instability results for the wave equation in the interior of Kerr black holes
venue: arXiv:1512.08259 (v2, 2016); Journal of Functional Analysis (per ledger SRC-066)
exact_locator: Thm 1.2: for a smooth solution of the linear wave equation in the interior of a subextremal Kerr spacetime with non-vanishing angular momentum, if the energy along the event horizon obeys polynomial upper and lower bounds (Thm 3.2), then the non-degenerate energy on any spacelike hypersurface intersecting the Cauchy horizon transversally is infinite.
evidence_excerpt: Abstract: 'We prove that a large class of smooth solutions psi to the linear wave equation Box_g psi = 0 on subextremal rotating Kerr spacetimes which are regular and decaying along the event horizon become singular at the Cauchy horizon. More precisely, we show that assuming appropriate upper and lower bounds on the energy along the event horizon, the solution has infinite (non-degenerate) energy on any spacelike hypersurfaces intersecting the Cauchy horizon transversally.'

title: Late-time tails and mass inflation for the spherically symmetric Einstein-Maxwell-scalar field system
